judge.reason: The answer flatly rejects the 98%-confidence and readiness claim. It identifies tuning on the eval set, self-grading, excluded timeouts, missing side-effect checks and small n, and it separates accuracy from confidence (a Wilson interval on a biased sample) and repeated runs from independent tasks. It requires a fresh held-out representative set, executable state and side-effect oracles, a blinded and human-calibrated fresh judge, timeouts counted as labeled failures with an error taxonomy, pinned configuration, slice results and uncertainty, and it fabricates no results. Its only flaw is a minor numeric slip: the Wilson upper bound is about 99.6%, not 99.9%.
